knowledge:
- key_parameters: genetable=A matrix or data frame of RNA-seq counts where rows represent genes and columns represent samples ;; design=A factor specifying the group assignment (e.g., "A" vs "B") for each sample ;; burn=The number of burn-in iterations for the MCMC sampler ;; reps=The number of MCMC repetitions/samples to draw after burn-in ;; printEvery=The interval at which progress is printed to the console ;; mode=Character string specifying output detail: "minimal" (returns posterior means and differential expression probabilities), "full" (returns full posterior distribution of log fold changes), or "extended" (returns posterior distributions for all parameters)
- alternatives: Negative binomial models such as edgeR or DESeq. BADER is preferred when a fully Bayesian approach is desired to quantify parameter uncertainty, especially in datasets with low sample sizes or strong overdispersion.
- when_to_use: When analyzing RNA-seq count data to identify differentially expressed genes between two groups, particularly when sample sizes are small and quantifying parameter uncertainty is important for downstream analyses like gene set enrichment.
- pitfalls: Using too few MCMC iterations (e.g., burn=1e3, reps=1e3) will lead to poor posterior estimates; higher values should be used for actual analyses. Failing to filter out genes with zero counts across all samples before running the algorithm.

workflows.name: bayesian_differential_expression
workflows.intent: Perform Bayesian differential expression analysis on RNA-seq count data to estimate posterior probabilities of differential expression and log fold changes, followed by gene set enrichment.
input: pasilla_gene_counts.tsv (tab-separated count matrix file where rows are genes and columns are samples)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the count data and define the experimental design factor. ;; 2. Filter out genes with zero counts across all samples and subset the dataset. ;; 3. Run the BADER MCMC sampler to estimate posterior probabilities. ;; 4. Extract posterior probabilities of differential expression and identify top genes. ;; 5. Run the BADER MCMC sampler in full mode to obtain the posterior distribution of log fold changes. ;; 6. Perform gene set enrichment analysis using the posterior distribution of log fold changes.
workflows.code:
library(BADER)
datafile <- system.file( "extdata/pasilla_gene_counts.tsv", package="pasilla" )
pasillaCountTable <- read.table( datafile, header=TRUE, row.names=1 )
head(pasillaCountTable)
genetable <- pasillaCountTable[,c(3,4,6,7)]
genetable <- genetable[rowSums(genetable) > 0,]
genetable <- genetable[1:500,]
design <- factor(c("A","A","B","B"))
set.seed(21)
results <- BADER(genetable,design,burn=1e3,reps=1e3,printEvery=1e3)
names(results)
rownames(genetable)[order(results$diffProb,decreasing=TRUE)[1:10]]
results <- BADER(genetable,design,mode="full",burn=1e3,reps=3e3,printEvery=1e3)
S <- c(1,2,3,51,52,53)
T <- c(54,55,56)
f <- function(sample,set)
    mean(sample[set] != 0) > mean(sample[-set] != 0)
mean(apply(results$logFoldChangeDist,1,f,set=S))
mean(apply(results$logFoldChangeDist,1,f,set=T))
